findings.reason: without `--project reckon` on the named command, §14's guarantee is never invoked and the node would run the unscoped destructive pass the hold exists to prevent.
findings.text: §5 says the pass "relies on §14, which scopes every gc sweep to the project it runs for" and requires "no removal line names a run that belongs to another project", but the command it names is the bare `reckon crew gc --apply`: `--project` defaults to `None` ("all local ledgers by default", `reckon/crew_run_commands.py:2219-2224`), and §14's deliverable scopes the sweeps only "With `--project P`", so the named pass still walks every local ledger and the done-when's own check would fail, which is exactly the return condition `c-hold-s5` set ("scoped to `--project reckon`")

findings.reason: as written the attribution rule cannot decide the index case, so the node is forced to guess the evidence the section was meant to fix.
findings.text: §14 requires the orphan ledger-index sweep to act only on entries belonging to P, and defines belonging as "its live pointer, manifest or run record names P", but a `ledger-*.sqlite` index carries none of these: `_orphan_ledger_indexes` identifies it only by `recorded_ledger_path` (`reckon/crew/gc.py:598-656`), so a literal implementation must either invent a fourth rule or report every index as `unknown`/kept, which contradicts the done-when's requirement that "gc --apply --project reckon removes only reckon's entries" including its orphan ledger index

findings.reason: the claim sends the node to re-scope a sweep that already meets the endpoint, and the plan's own done-when gives that case no failing base arm to prove the change was needed.
findings.text: §14's Why says "Two sweeps in the same call are unscoped too, `_orphan_ledger_indexes` and `_stale_run_locks`", but `_stale_run_locks` already offers only a lock whose run id is in `ledgered` (`reckon/crew/routing.py:2055`) and `ledgered` is built from `_gc_projects(repo_root, project)`, which returns only the named project when `--project` is given (`reckon/crew/gc.py:82-89`), so it cannot remove another project's lock today, and the done-when correctly shows no base arm for that case

response_events.note: §5's commands are now reckon crew gc --project reckon, report-only and --apply, with the reason the flag is required
§14 now defines index ownership: a ledger index belongs to P when its recorded_ledger_path is P's own ledger

rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §14's done-when requires the orphan ledger-index sweep to attribute an index to a project, but the deliverable's attribution rule names only a live pointer, manifest or run record, none of which a `ledger-*.sqlite` carries.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — §5 moves every command to an `all_debug` job under `env -u SLURM_JOB_ID` and writes logs under the run directory, and §14 puts its logs under the run directory, both durable paths.

rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §5's done-when claims the pass relies on §14's project scoping while the command it names passes no `--project`, so the scoping it depends on never engages, and §14's Why names the stale run-lock sweep as deleting another project's locks when that sweep is already restricted to the selected project's ledger.
